tasks.subject: Task 1: Pin git shut, add bytes-mode call
tasks.description:
**Goal:** No git call this module makes can be sent down a lazy fetch that execs a repository-configured transport, and a caller can read a blob without `subprocess` raising on non-UTF-8 bytes.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/git_added_lines.py:20-63`
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py` (append test class)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `_git` passes `-c protocol.allow=never` and sets `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in the subprocess environment
- [ ] `-c diff.noprefix=false` and `-c diff.mnemonicPrefix=false` are gone
- [ ] `-c core.quotePath=false` and `-c core.fsmonitor=false` remain
- [ ] `_git_bytes(cwd, *args)` exists and returns `(rc, bytes)`; `_git` still returns `(rc, str)`
- [ ] Both share one implementation, and both keep the `--no-optional-locks` 129-retry behaviour
- [ ] A partial-clone fixture with a missing blob and a `core.sshCommand` sentinel runs `cat-file blob` and the sentinel is never created
- [ ] `_git`'s docstring no longer claims the pins protect a diff parser

**Verify:** `python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py -v` -> OK

Full step-by-step code is in the plan under "Task 1". The `LazyFetchCannotExec` test body and the complete replacement `_git`/`_git_bytes`/`_git_call` implementation are given verbatim there.

CRITICAL: the pins are best-effort hardening, NOT a completeness claim. The property actually relied on is that no call converts worktree content or fetches a missing object. `protocol.allow=never` and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` are independent mechanisms; apply BOTH.

tasks.subject: Task 2: Replace worktree diff with raw blob compare
tasks.description:
**Goal:** The tracked-path branch derives added lines without asking git to convert worktree content, and an unanswerable question skips the path instead of scanning the whole file.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/git_added_lines.py:114-193` (and the import at `:17`)
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py` (append test classes)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] No `git diff` call remains anywhere in `git_added_lines.py`
- [ ] `rel` comes from `ls-files -z --full-name --error-unmatch`, never from `os.path.relpath`
- [ ] Absence from `HEAD` is established by `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD:<rel>` returning rc 1 - not by `cat-file` failing
- [ ] `HEAD` existence is cached on the worktree ROOT (not the submitted path's directory); a repository with no commits skips the path
- [ ] The blob is read via `_git_bytes`, capped at `READ_CAP_BYTES`, decoded with `errors="replace"`
- [ ] A `HEAD` blob containing a non-UTF-8 byte yields only the genuinely added line — today that path returns `{}`, so this widens coverage
- [ ] A tracked file with `filter.x.process` set produces correct added lines and no sentinel; same for `filter.x.clean`, as a separate fixture
- [ ] A staged-new file yields its whole content; the same path under `vendor/` is skipped and counted in `vendored_skipped`
- [ ] A worktree root reached through a symlink still resolves and scans
- [ ] Two files in different subdirectories of ONE worktree probe `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD` exactly once

**Verify:** `python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py -v` -> OK

Full code is in the plan under "Task 2": the `_repo` fixture builder, five test classes, and the `_head_exists` / `_tracked_added_lines` helpers plus the exact replacement block.

AFTER-GATE CORRECTIONS: (1) `_head_exists(cwd, root, cache)` keys on the worktree ROOT, not the directory asked from. (2) The Latin-1 fixture fails by returning `{}`, NOT the whole file — today the diff output carries the byte, `text=True` raises, `_git` returns `(127, "")` and the path is dropped. Reading bytes is what makes it scannable at all.

THE CRITICAL DETAIL: never infer "not in HEAD" from `cat-file` failing. That folds a decode error, a timeout and an unfetchable blob into "every line is new", which blocks a close on comments the implementer never wrote. Only `rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD:<rel>` rc 1 licenses treating the file as new. Also: `os.path.relpath` against `--show-toplevel` is wrong whenever a parent is a symlink.

```json:metadata
{"files": ["plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/git_added_lines.py", "plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py"], "verifyCommand": "python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py -v", "acceptanceCriteria": ["no git diff call remains", "rel from ls-files --full-name", "positive rev-parse HEAD:<rel> probe", "HEAD existence cached on the worktree root", "blob read as bytes and capped", "non-UTF-8 blob yields only the added line (today it returns {})", "filter.process and filter.clean fixtures create no sentinel", "staged-new whole file, vendored staged-new skipped", "symlinked worktree root resolves"], "modelTier": "standard"}
```

tasks.subject: Task 3: Honour content-conversion attributes
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A `filter`-attributed path is skipped rather than reported as wholly new, and a `working-tree-encoding` path keeps being scanned by decoding with the declared codec.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan.py:24-66` (`read_text_capped`)
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/git_added_lines.py` (new `_converted` helper + call site)
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py` (append test class)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `read_text_capped(path, encoding=None)` decodes with `encoding` when given, `utf-8` otherwise
- [ ] An unknown codec name makes `read_text_capped` return `None`
- [ ] `git check-attr -z filter working-tree-encoding -- <rel>` is consulted once per tracked path
- [ ] A path whose `filter` attribute names a driver is skipped; a BARE `filter` (reported as `set`) is NOT — it names no driver and runs nothing (verified)
- [ ] A path with `working-tree-encoding=UTF-16` still yields its genuine `// fixes #1`
- [ ] A `check-attr` that fails to answer skips the path — including an rc-0 response that is empty, truncated, or names a different path
- [ ] No call added here runs a filter
- [ ] `ContentFiltersAreNeverRun` from Task 2 is UPDATED here, not left to fail: those fixtures route `*.go` to `filter=x`, which is exactly the skip condition this task introduces
- [ ] A new test pins the blob read's own no-conversion property with the attribute probe bypassed, since the skip now shadows it

**Verify:** `python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py -v` -> OK

Full code is in the plan under "Task 3", including `check-attr -z` output parsing (records are path\0attr\0value\0 triples).

THE TRAP THIS TASK MUST NOT FALL INTO: Task 2's `ContentFiltersAreNeverRun` asserts added lines for a fixture whose `.gitattributes` routes `*.go` to `filter=x` — precisely the skip condition introduced here. Those tests break unless this task updates them; plan Step 3 moves the expectation to `{}` and KEEPS the sentinel assertion. Once the skip exists no ordinary fixture can reach the blob comparison for a filtered path, so `BlobReadConvertsNothingWithoutTheSkip` pins that property by stubbing `_converted` open.

WHY THE TWO ATTRIBUTES DIFFER: `filter` cannot be recovered - comparing a pointer/ciphertext in HEAD against worktree content requires running the filter command, the one thing this module refuses to do. `working-tree-encoding` CAN be recovered and must not be skipped: its value IS the codec name, so decoding costs a `codecs.lookup`, not a subprocess. Skipping it would give up a detection that works today, and give it up silently.

tasks.subject: Task 4: Starred lines need an open block comment
tasks.description:
**Goal:** A `*`-led line inside a raw string literal stops being scanned as a block-comment continuation, without losing any detection that works today.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan.py:157-190` (`comment_spans`) and `:370-391` (`violations`)
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py` (append test class)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `block_comment_lines(text)` returns line texts for which a block was ALREADY open at the line's start (continuations); a line that opens a block partway through itself is deliberately excluded
- [ ] A `${…}` hole inside a backtick span returns to code state (today's scanner catches `${ compute() /* fixes #1 */ }` — losing it is a regression); nested braces do not end the hole early
- [ ] Single- and double-quoted spans end at end of line; a lone `'` opens nothing
- [ ] Backtick and triple-quoted spans do cross newlines
- [ ] `comment_spans(path, raw, allow_star=True)` falls through to the normal walk when `allow_star` is False
- [ ] `violations(path, added_lines, context=None)` computes the walk lazily and caches it per call
- [ ] A walk that raises falls back to today's behaviour rather than dropping the scan
- [ ] `context=None` behaves exactly as before
- [ ] SCOPE LIMIT: matching is by line TEXT, not position (the close-time caller has no indices), so a line whose exact text appears both inside a real block AND inside a raw string still fires — conservative, same as today, not a regression
- [ ] Go raw string and Kotlin triple-quoted fixtures yield `[]`; a KDoc `/** * fixes #1 */` still yields a violation (a bare tracker key is NOT usable — there is no default tracker tell)
- [ ] A Rust lifetime, a JSX apostrophe, a C `#error` apostrophe and a JS regex literal each followed by a genuine `/** * fixes #1 */` all still fire

**Verify:** `python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/comment_scan_test.py -v` -> OK

USE THE `block_comment_lines` BODY IN THE PLAN VERBATIM — prototyped and proven against 12 fixtures (all pass, 60k lines in 0.38s). In particular backtick spans are scanned character by character, not jumped with `find`: jumping misses a `${` later on the same line. Full code is in the plan under "Task 4": four test classes, the complete `block_comment_lines` state machine, `starred_candidate`, the `comment_spans` signature change, and the rewritten `violations` body.

THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: single- and double-quoted spans END AT END OF LINE. Without it one stray apostrophe - a Rust lifetime, an apostrophe in JSX text, a C `#error don't` - opens a span that runs to end of file and suppresses every genuine block comment after it. Today's per-line `_quotes_balanced` confines that damage to one line, so getting this wrong is a REGRESSION. Only backtick and triple-quoted forms cross a newline. DO NOT WRITE THE KDOC TEST WITH A BARE TRACKER KEY. `_ticket_tell()` returns `None` unless `ANTI_TANGENT_TICKET_PATTERN` is set, so an unconfigured project has no tracker tell at all. Measured: `' * ABC-1234: widen the parser'` -> `[]`, `' * fixes #1'` -> a hit.

`block_lines is True` is the sentinel for "the walk failed, keep the old answer", distinct from a legitimately empty set.

tasks.subject: Task 6: fp-scan --ticket-pattern mode
tasks.description:
**Goal:** An operator can find out what `ANTI_TANGENT_TICKET_PATTERN` would newly block in this repository before committing to it.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py:36-46` and `:83-93`

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] With no flag, the env var is popped exactly as today, and stdout AND stderr are proven byte-identical to the pre-change version with `cmp` (not merely rc 0)
- [ ] `--ticket-pattern <regex>` sets the variable instead, before `comment_scan` is imported
- [ ] A pattern that `_ticket_tell()` would silently drop (bad regex, over the length cap) exits non-zero with a message, rather than reporting a clean run
- [ ] In `--ticket-pattern` mode the stderr summary reports total hits AND how many carry the ticket tell; in default mode the existing one-number summary is preserved byte-for-byte
- [ ] A missing argument to the flag exits non-zero

**Verify:**
```bash
python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "default rc=$?"
python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py --ticket-pattern '[A-Z]{2,}-[0-9]+' >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "flag rc=$?"
python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py --ticket-pattern '(' >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "bad-regex rc=$? (want 2)"
python3 plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-scan.py --ticket-pattern >/dev/null 2>&1; echo "missing-arg rc=$? (want 2)"
```
Then `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/fp-report.sh` must give the same verdict as on `main`.

Full code is in the plan under "Task 6".

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: `comment_scan` binds the ticket tell at import time (`_ticket = _ticket_tell()`). Parse argv and set the environment BEFORE the `from comment_scan import ...` line, or the flag silently does nothing. Validate by asking the module what it actually bound (`comment_scan._ticket is None`) rather than re-implementing its rules, which would drift.

tasks.subject: Task 7: Hook-level evals for both exec paths
tasks.description:
**Goal:** Prove end-to-end through `check-task-complete` that neither exec path runs - by observing the eval suite green with the protections in place, AND red (`file must not exist: .../SENTINEL`) with each protection removed in turn.

> **USER-ORDERED GATE - NON-SKIPPABLE.** This task was requested by the user in the current conversation. It MUST NOT be closed by walking around it, by declaring it "verified inline", or by substituting a cheaper check. Close only after every item in `acceptanceCriteria` has been re-validated independently, with output captured.

A green suite alone does not close this task. An eval that passes whether or not the bug is present is not a test, and these three exist solely to catch a regression in the one property this release claims. Both observations - protections on, protections removed - must be captured.

**Files:**
- Modify: `plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/guard-evals.json` (append to `.evals`)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] Three new cases: `filter.x.clean`, `filter.x.process`, and the partial-clone lazy fetch
- [ ] Each points the repository-configured command at a sentinel file and asserts it via `expected_file_absent`
- [ ] Each expects exit 0 - the added line carries no tell, so only an executed command can change the outcome
- [ ] Every new case has a `reason` saying what it would catch if it regressed
- [ ] Ids continue from the current maximum
- [ ] Captured output shows the suite GREEN with protections in place
- [ ] Captured output shows each case RED when its protection is removed, then restored
- [ ] The filter mutation disables BOTH `_converted`'s skip and the blob comparison — the skip fires first, so mutating only the comparison leaves the case green and proves nothing

**Verify:** `bash plugin/anti-tangent-guard/evals/run.sh` -> all cases pass; then re-run with each protection removed and capture the RED output before restoring.

Full generator script is in the plan under "Task 7", Step 2.

MECHANISM: the harness already supports this. `expected_file_absent: [paths]` (`evals/run.sh:664-688`) fails a case if any listed path exists after the hook ran, with `{{TMPDIR}}` substituted; eval 88 uses it for the symlink case. Assert the sentinel directly - do not infer execution from the exit code.

THE MUTATION MUST REMOVE EVERY LAYER, NOT THE LAST ONE. After Task 3 a filter-attributed path is skipped by `_converted` BEFORE the comparison runs, so restoring the old `git diff` alone leaves the case green — a mutation that looks like proof and is the opposite. For the filter cases disable both: make `_converted` return `(False, None)` unconditionally AND put the old diff call back — using `":(top)" + rel` as the pathspec, since `_tracked_added_lines(parent, rel, new_text)` has no `path` in scope and a bare `rel` silently matches nothing from a subdirectory (rc 0, no output, no filter: a false green). The RED must be specifically `file must not exist: .../SENTINEL`; any other failure means the mutation never reached the filter. For the lazy-fetch case drop BOTH `-c protocol.allow=never` and `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH`, since either alone still blocks the fetch. Restore with `git checkout plugin/anti-tangent-guard/hooks/git_added_lines.py`, confirm green, then commit.
